Theme

Nature & food

wild adjective

of animals: not tame

also wild animal, wild animals, wild beast, untamed, game (wild animals)

classical

Cic. N.D. 2.99: bēstiārum vel cicurum vel ferārum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 407

ferus, fera, ferum

wild, untamed

Opposed to cicur, tame. Of land it is untilled, and of people savage, fierce, cruel (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • fera, ferae f. — a wild animal, a wild beast

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.50: neque ūllā rē longius absumus ā nātūrā ferārum (Lewis & Short)

    The adjective used as a noun (bēstia understood): the usual word for a wild animal, and also for game as food (Tac. Germ. 23.1, under wild, of plants).

Examples

  • in bēstiīs, volucribus, nantibus, agrestibus, cicuribus, ferīs

    in animals: birds, creatures that swim, beasts of the field, tame and wildCic. Amic. 81

  • calumniārī sī quis autem voluerit, quod arborēs loquantur, nōn tantum ferae, fictīs jocārī nōs meminerit fābulīs

    and if anyone wants to carp because trees talk, not only wild beasts, let him remember that we are joking in made-up storiesPhaedr. 1 prol. 5–7

See also wild, wild, wild boar.

SourcesLewis & Short: ferus · Lewis & Short: cicur
